transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-09-22T15:00:00Z
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Lena Park (AE), Omar Singh (SE), Maya Chen (Solutions Engineer) \u2014 Zenith Tech: Rajesh Patel (CTO), Emily Ortiz (Lead ML Engineer), Tom Wu (Product)

Summary: quick demo of Redwood structured output (json mode) and function calling, show guardrails + schema enforcement, discuss hosted vs dedicated and security reqs around kms and audit logs

[00:00] Lena Park: hey thanks for joining everyone, we'll keep this pretty tight. i'm lena, AE at Redwood, with omar and maya from the solutions team. hows your morning rajesh?
[00:12] Rajesh Patel: good, thanks. excited to see the structured output flow, we have a pretty strict schema requirement for our finance ingestion pipeline.
[00:22] Omar Singh: great, quick agenda \u2014 api demo of json mode, console walkthrough for Optimize suggestions, then function/tool calling to show guarded execution and validation. we'll also touch on security and next steps.
[00:38] Emily Ortiz: couple of constraints upfront \u2014 we need deterministic json: keys in a schema, strict types, and failure modes that are safe (no partial writes). we also need KMS integration for encryption at rest.
[00:50] Maya Chen: totally understood. we'll demo Redwood's structured output mode which can take a json schema and enforce it at generation time, plus validation and fallback behaviors: either strict reject, auto-correct with confidence threshold, or map to a safe error payload.
[01:05] Tom Wu: curious about function calling \u2014 can it call our internal enrichment service without leaking PII to 3rd parties?
[01:12] Omar Singh: yes, we can route calls to your private functions in a VPC \u2014 the function calling demo will show a local webhook invocation. also the call metadata and logs are kept in your private audit logs when you're on Dedicated or Private.
[01:28] Lena Park: quick note \u2014 i'll flag the security whitepaper and SOC2 link in the follow-up.

[01:40] Demo start
[01:42] Omar Singh: ok i'm switching to the console, this is the structured output tab. here you paste a json schema (he pastes a schema) and select enforcement: strict | best-effort | audit-only. I'm going to pick strict for the demo.
[02:05] Om: this schema defines top-level fields: transaction_id (string), amount (number), currency (string, iso3), merchant (object with name, id), and risk_score (number 0-1). we also set a max tokens and streaming off for deterministic output.
[02:26] [audio glitch, brief \"uh-huh\"]
[02:30] Omar Singh: i'm calling the text generation api with json_mode:true and schema_id: txn_v1. the response should either be exactly the JSON or an error with structured error payload.
[02:45] Emily Ortiz: if the model hallucinates a field name, will it be removed or transformed? we can't accept unknown keys.
[02:52] Omar Singh: in strict mode unknown keys are rejected, you'll get status: invalid_schema_violation plus a rejected_fields list. we also log the raw output for audit. in best-effort mode we attempt to coerce types (e.g., \"100\" -> 100) if confidence high.
[03:10] Live response \u2014 console shows a JSON payload that matches schema exactly. small lag, then 200 ok and body is JSON.
[03:22] Rajesh Patel: looks good, but what about partial outputs when the token cutoff happens? we can't have truncated json saved by downstream.
[03:30] Omar Singh: Redwood's runtime does a final schema validation on the assembled streaming buffer; if the json is incomplete due to token limit, it returns a validation_error and empty body (or you can configure a fallback partial policy). we surface a specific error code so your ingestion can retry or drop.
[03:52] Tom Wu: what's the overhead for strict mode? will latency blow up?
[03:58] Maya Chen: small overhead from the validator (milliseconds) and maybe extra tokens if best-effort correction is used, but latency tradeoff is minimal vs the cost of downstream fixes. our Optimize tab also suggests batching and quantization profiles per model to keep token cost low.

[04:18] Function calling demo
[04:20] Omar Singh: now switching to function-calling example. we show a prompt that asks to enrich merchant info by calling your enrichment service. in Redwood we have two modes: managed function (you register an endpoint) or local isolated function (calls stay within your VPC).
[04:38] Emily Ortiz: for compliance we need that call never exits our network. can you do on-prem or VPC-only?
[04:44] Omar Singh: yes, with Dedicated or Private we can configure the egress rules; the function execution happens on instances inside your network, we don't proxy payloads through Redwood's public control plane in that configuration.
[04:58] Om: triggering the function now, schema for enrichment defined: merchant.id -> enrichment API returns merchant.name, category, risk_score. the runtime validates the function response against the declared schema before returning to the client.
[05:20] [slight crosstalk]
[05:24] Maya Chen: important guardrail: we sign function payloads and can also strip PII fields if requested via a pre-processing hook. you can also set a whitelist of endpoints.
[05:36] Rajesh Patel: error handling \u2014 what if enrichment API times out? we need a graceful fallback so our ingestion doesn't block.
[05:44] Omar Singh: you configure per-route timeouts and fallback policies. typical pattern: enrich call times out -> return partial record with enrichment:null and a warning field plus a unique trace id for debugging. all such events are logged in the Console and tied to the request id.

[06:05] Security + compliance discussion
[06:06] Lena Park: just to summarize security \u2014 SOC2 Type II, customer-managed KMS for Private, audit logs exported to your S3 or SIEM, SSO/SAML + RBAC.
[06:16] Emily Ortiz: are the audit logs tamper-proof? we need integrity checks.
[06:20] Maya Chen: we support log signing and append-only storage options; also audit events include per-request model, schema_id, route, and function call metadata.
[06:35] Rajesh Patel: great. also want to confirm data residency \u2014 EU vs US regions.
[06:40] Omar Singh: region pinning available for both hosted and Dedicated; Private gives you full on-prem option. we'll note region in the pilot proposal.

[06:52] Pricing & pilot
[06:53] Lena Park: proposed pilot \u2014 2-week sandbox: hosted sandbox with dedicated routing, sample capacity for X tokens/day, Redwood will run three schema/guardrail tests: strict, best-effort, and audit-only. we'll produce a benchmark sheet with success rate and latency per request.
[07:12] Rajesh Patel: timeline looks good. once we see the benchmark we'll decide on dedicated vs hosted.

[07:20] Questions from customer
[07:22] Tom Wu: can we get a recording of the function-calling segment?
[07:25] Lena Park: yes will share recording and the console exports.

[07:30] Wrap and recap
[07:31] Lena Park: recap of next steps: send pilot proposal + pricing, security docs (SOC2, KMS integration steps, log export), and schedule kickoff. action items captured. Thanks everyone.
[07:47] Rajesh Patel: thanks all.

End transcript.
